components: UrlValidator (extend: scheme allowlist, credentials, IP/private range checks, blocklist with subdomain match, DNS resolution check)
HostBlocklist (config-backed set of malicious domains, suffix match)
ShortenerService (expiry validation, resolve with Expired status, expiry reporting)
IUrlRepository/InMemoryUrlRepository (cache-friendly lookup via ConcurrentDictionary; expiry stored on ShortLink)
ClickRecorder/ClickProcessor (bounded Channel, DropWrite on full, background consumer, errors swallowed)
RateLimit middleware/policies (per-IP, separate creation and redirect policies, Retry-After, configurable)
ShortenerOptions (limits, queue capacity, blocklist, expiry, trusted proxies)
Contracts (response includes expiry and expired flag)

endpoints.summary: Create short link with validated target and optional UTC expiry; rate limited
302 redirect to target; enqueue click non-blocking; 410 if expired; rate limited
Existing legacy redirect, same behavior as /r/{code}
Link metadata: target, created, expiry, expired flag

dataModel: ShortLink: Code, TargetUrl, CreatedAt (UTC), ExpiresAt (UTC, nullable), Active flag (existing)
Options: CreateLimitPerMinute=30, RedirectLimitPerMinute=600, AnalyticsQueueCapacity, Blocklist[], DnsTimeout, TrustedProxies[]
risks: DNS rebinding: creation-time resolution can differ later; redirects are client-side so server SSRF is limited, but document it
DNS lookups at creation can be slow; apply timeout and fail closed
Bounded queue drops clicks under overload, so analytics can undercount (accepted trade-off)
In-memory state is lost on restart and is not shared across instances; rate limits are per-instance
Per-IP limiting behind proxies needs trusted-proxy config or all clients look the same
Fixed-window limiter allows boundary bursts; sliding window costs more
Stale clock or time zone bugs in expiry; use UTC and an injectable clock
The p95 < 50 ms target must be verified with a real load test, which is environment-dependent
Rate limiter memory growth from many IPs; needs window eviction

decisions.decision: Use a bounded Channel with DropWrite and a background consumer for clicks
decisions.rationale: Keeps the redirect path non-blocking and unaffected by a slow or failing sink
decisions.alternative: Unbounded queue or synchronous write, rejected because of memory risk and latency

decisions.decision: Static configurable blocklist with suffix matching
decisions.rationale: Matches the stated assumption; no external dependency or latency

decisions.decision: Per-IP partitioned rate limiting with separate policies for create and redirect
decisions.rationale: Isolates clients and allows independent configuration
decisions.alternative: Global limit, which lets one client affect others

decisions.decision: Resolve and validate DNS at creation, rejecting any private result
Use 302 and return 410 for expired links; count only successful 302s
decisions.rationale: Honors expiry and keeps analytics accurate
decisions.alternative: 301 permanent redirect, which is cached by clients

impact.reason: Add scheme, credential, private-range, DNS and blocklist checks
Expiry validation, expired resolve status, click enqueue only on success
Map 410/429/400, apply rate limit policies, Retry-After
Expose expiry and expired flag; accept expiry on create
Bounded channel, non-blocking writes, failure isolation
Add limits, queue capacity, blocklist, trusted proxies

dataFlows: Create: client -> rate limiter -> endpoint -> UrlValidator (scheme, credentials, blocklist, DNS/private check) -> expiry check -> repository -> 201
Redirect: client -> rate limiter -> repository lookup -> expiry/active check -> 302 and TryWrite ClickEvent to channel (non-blocking)
Analytics: channel -> ClickProcessor background consumer -> AnalyticsStore -> GET analytics
